findings.element: "Use a custom rule for this integration" toggle description, and step 5 of "In plain terms"
findings.finding: The outcome for a payment the rule fails to match is only ever called "processed as usual", one sentence after being told the default matcher "never runs" — so "as usual" has no meaning left, and the copy never says in words that a new invoice or sales receipt gets created for that payment.
findings.user_impact: The owner who came here because payments were creating duplicates reads "processed as usual" as the safe option, leaves "Cancel sync" off, and gets exactly the duplicate records the rule was supposed to stop.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "processed as usual" with the concrete result — e.g. "Synder creates a new sales receipt for the payment instead of putting it on an existing invoice" — in both the toggle description and the plain-terms step.

evidence.quote: If the rule finds nothing, the payment is processed as usual (or the sync is cancelled, below).
evidence.source: plain-language — the phrase is unexplained and contradicts the preceding "never runs … not even as a fallback" in the same paragraph

findings.element: Section 1, invoice-number row — "Metadata key" field (placeholder "e.g. invoices") and its validation message
findings.finding: "Metadata key" is developer vocabulary with no explanation of what a key is or where to find the one this store actually uses, yet the rule cannot be saved until the field is filled in correctly.
findings.user_impact: A bookkeeper picks "Payment metadata" because the hint recommends it for simple charges, then hits a blocking error they have no way to resolve, and abandons the setup rather than guess a value that silently matches nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Label it in the user's terms ("Which Stripe field holds the invoice reference?"), and add one line saying where to find it plus a "Learn more" link, or offer the known keys as a list instead of free text.

evidence.quote: Enter the metadata key to match on.
evidence.source: plain-language — "metadata" and "key" appear nowhere in vocabulary.md and are not explained on screen

findings.element: Section 3 "What happens after that" — "No matching open invoice was found" row description
findings.finding: The consequence of switching this on is stated as "nothing is created" with no word on where the payment then goes, whether the transaction is still in Synder, or whether it can be synced later once the invoice exists.
findings.user_impact: The owner reads "nothing is created" as "my payment is thrown away", so they leave the setting off to be safe and accept duplicates instead of the outcome they wanted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the reassurance next to the toggle: the payment stays in Synder with a Canceled status and can be synced again once a matching invoice exists — nothing is deleted from your books.

evidence.quote: On: nothing is created. Off: the payment is processed as usual.
evidence.source: plain-language — missing reassurance; vocabulary.md status list has "Canceled" for platform transactions, which this copy never surfaces

gaps: Save confirmation: the slice records no toast or post-save copy, so I cannot judge whether the user is told the rule is live and what it now affects.
Cancel: no copy is recorded for leaving the overlay with unsaved edits, so whether the user is warned about losing a half-built rule is unknown.
Hover-only text is not in the inventory — the locked "Compare against" field carries an explanatory title attribute that never appears as visible copy.

Starter (gated) state: no upsell or blocked-click copy is recorded, so what a Starter user is told is unknown. (Orchestrator note: the state map records the Configure button as disabled on Starter, so the agent's inference that it is 'active' is wrong.)
